output.brief: The rejections trace to a data error on our side, not to the fungicide, the Lower Serra growers or Meridane. When Meridane bookings moved to the new documentation system, the mandarin product record was copied from avocado. It carries 7.0°C instead of our 4.0°C specification. Every Meridane container since go-live (K3, K4, K6, K8, K9) was sent at 7.0°C. The units held that setpoint closely. All five were rejected. The 4.0°C containers, including three on Pellacor fungicide, all passed. Fruit that was old-stock fungicide at 7.0°C (K3) also failed, so the new fungicide is not the cause. Lower Serra fruit did show more decay inside the rejected containers. That is a secondary effect and not established as a cause. Next steps: correct the product record to 4.0°C now. Ask Meridane to reset the container at sea (sailed 3 Oct) and the one queued for 10 Oct. Add a check that compares reefer settings with the product specification before submission. Do not suspend growers, withhold payments, switch back the fungicide or file the refrigeration claim. Loggers in containers are a reasonable extra. I'm quite sure of this diagnosis.
